statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, len(r) = n and for every i with 0 <= i < n the following holds. Let S_i = { j | 0 <= j < n and i lies on the unique simple path from 0 to j in the tree }; this is the subtree of i when the tree is rooted at 0. If |S_i| < 3, then r[i] = 1. If |S_i| >= 3, let P_i = max{ cost[a] * cost[b] * cost[c] | a,b,c are pairwise distinct nodes in S_i }; then r[i] = max(0, P_i).
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with both entries in {0,...,n-1}; the undirected graph on vertices {0,...,n-1} whose edges are the pairs {edges[k][0], edges[k][1]} for 0 <= k < n-1 is a tree; and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000.

statement: Under these preconditions, placed_coins returns a result r; it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or a panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with both entries in {0,...,n-1}; the undirected graph on vertices {0,...,n-1} whose edges are the pairs {edges[k][0], edges[k][1]} for 0 <= k < n-1 is a tree; and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000.

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, len(r) = n. Equivalently, there is exactly one coin entry for each node label 0,1,...,n-1.
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with both entries in {0,...,n-1}; the graph formed by edges is a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= r[i] <= 1000000000000 (10^12).
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n and |S_i| >= 3, for all pairwise distinct nodes a,b,c in S_i, cost[a] * cost[b] * cost[c] <= r[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if |S_i| >= 3 and r[i] > 0, then there exist pairwise distinct nodes a,b,c in S_i such that cost[a] * cost[b] * cost[c] = r[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n and |S_i| >= 3, r[i] = 0 if and only if for every pairwise distinct a,b,c in S_i, cost[a] * cost[b] * cost[c] < 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.

statement: Whenever placed_coins edges cost returns r and placed_coins edges' cost returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i. Also assume edges' is any permutation of the list edges (so edges' describes the same undirected tree).

statement: Whenever placed_coins returns a result r, for all nodes i,j with 0 <= i,j < n, if i lies on the unique path from 0 to j (i is an ancestor of j, possibly i = j), |S_i| >= 3, and |S_j| >= 3, then r[i] >= r[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(cost). Assume 2 <= n <= 20000; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a vector of length 2 with entries in {0,...,n-1}; edges form a tree on {0,...,n-1}; and 1 <= |cost[i]| <= 10000 for every i.
